mechanism_narrative: Elevated federal funds rates above 5.0% compress equity valuations through higher discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between high rates and negative equity returns
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation above 3.5% (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) triggers aggressive central bank tightening, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:Inflation-driven rate hikes historically precede equity drawdowns
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Joint rise in federal funds rates and decline in unemployment signal a late-cycle economy prone to recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE produces positive SPX 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Early-cycle labor market recovery, defined by rising employment and falling unemployment, drives S&P 500 positive returns as economic growth accelerates over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is rising and UNRATE is falling.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Housing starts are a leading indicator for economic growth
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is rising.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
evidence_refs: fact:Industrial production declines often precede equity market downturns
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth combined with rising retail sales (GDPC1 and RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of strong GDPC1 growth and rising RSAFS produces negative SPX 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), S&P 500 forward returns are negative over 20 days as inflation control measures weigh on equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%).
